prerequisites: A Plinth account — Google sign-in or an email link at /account. No card for the free tier.
Nothing at all for GET /api/search, which resolves a name to an EIN un-keyed and unmetered.

plans.name: Free ($0)
plans.requiredFor: 50 REST calls a month across /grants/* and the organization endpoints. No POST /api/sql, no connector.

plans.name: For non-profits ($75/month)
plans.requiredFor: 50 REST calls a month, plus unlimited plain-English analysis.

plans.name: For consultants ($250/month)
plans.requiredFor: 10,000 REST calls a month, plus POST /api/sql, the people/board and asset tables, and the MCP connector.

mechanisms.description: Entity resolution is open: GET /api/search takes a name and returns EIN, kind, state and the canonical page URL with no key and no metering. It is the intended first call.
The REST key is minted by a signed-in human at /account (one key per account, rotatable, shown once). There is no programmatic issue endpoint.

The MCP connector accepts RFC 7591 dynamic client registration — an agent registers itself, then runs authorization_code + PKCE S256 against the endpoints in our RFC 8414 metadata. The account it authorizes must be on a plan that includes the connector.

methods.bootstrap: A human signs in at /account once and mints the key; after that nothing is manual.

fields.api_key: Plinth API key, sent as X-API-Key or Authorization: Bearer

credentials.rotation: Rotate at /account; rotating retires the previous key immediately.

fields.access_token: OAuth access token for the MCP endpoint

credentials.rotation: Refresh via the token endpoint; revoke by removing the connector.

scopes.notes: Plan-gated rather than scoped. The free tier reads /grants/* and the organization endpoints; POST /api/sql, the people/board and asset tables and the MCP connector require a paid plan. A request outside the plan answers 402 with a message naming the reason.

economics.freeTier: 50 REST calls a month on a free key, three plain-English questions a day, and unmetered GET /api/search. Paid plans raise the REST allowance to 10,000 a month.

gaps: No programmatic signup: an agent cannot create a Plinth account without a browser sign-in.
No management API for keys — issue and rotation happen in the account dashboard only.
The REST API authenticates with a static key rather than OAuth; only the MCP endpoint is OAuth 2.1.
No sandbox environment: the free tier IS the trial, against live data.
